title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Playbook for Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage
author: Riley Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Applied ML evaluation workflows used at Redwood Inference. It describes the standard processes for: onboarding models into the eval harness, constructing and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quantization profiles, establishing quality guardrails, and running regression triage. The goal is a single, repeatable, auditable flow that balances developer velocity with production safety.

Scope

- Applies to all models intended for any Redwood serving surface (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers functional correctness, safety, latency/quality tradeoffs under quantization, and regression detection.
- Does not replace product-specific acceptance criteria; teams must add product-specific tests where required.

Roles & Ownership

- Applied ML (owner): maintains the eval harness, prompt catalog, quantization profiling tools, and coordinates triage. (Primary: applied-ml@redwood.com)
- Model Owner (owner): responsible for onboarding artifacts, prompt validation, and responding to triage.
- Infra/Runtime (stakeholder): ensures runtime metrics (latency, OOMs) are tracked during profiling and rollouts.
- Product / Safety (stakeholder): provides acceptance criteria for guardrails and safety tests.

Principles

1. Single source of truth: every model has one canonical prompt set and one quantization profile per target deployment class.
2. Reproducibility: runs should be deterministic given seed and harness config.
3. Early detection: run regression checks on every model roll and quantization artifact.
4. Clear escalation: every failed test has an owner and a documented triage window.

Onboarding workflow (high-level)

1. Create model onboarding ticket and attach model metadata: architecture, weights location (S3/GCS), training dataset notes, and intended use-cases.
2. Populate required onboarding docs: model card, risk assessment, and initial prompt set (see Prompt Set subsection).
3. Run baseline eval harness (accuracy, calibration, latency) on float32 model. Record outputs to eval registry.
4. Generate quantization profile(s) (INT8/4-bit variants) and run quantization-aware evals.
5. Compare quantized results to baseline via the regression criteria. If within thresholds, promote quantized artifact to staging; otherwise, open regression triage.

Prompt sets and benchmarks

- Catalog: prompt sets are stored under the prompt catalog (/data/eval/prompt-sets) and referenced by canonical id.
- Structure: each prompt set must include: id, description, domain, list of prompts, expected behavior/labels, and example ground-truth where applicable.

Prompt set template (text table):

| field | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | ps_qa_support_001 | short id, kebab-case |
| description | Support ticket triage examples | 1-line summary |
| domain | support / triage | primary domain |
| seed_prompts | 200 queries | recommended min size: 200 |
| metric | EM / Rouge / BLEU / custom classifier | primary metric(s) |

- Coverage requirements: include edge cases, prompt prefixes (system/user), and prompt variations (typos, long context).
- Label quality: labels must be reviewed by two humans or one human + automated sanity checks.

Eval harness: standards & commands

- Harness: uses the standardized eval-harness service (service name: eval-harness), which runs tests in dockerized jobs and writes results to the eval registry (s3://redwood-evals/results/).
- Minimum outputs: per-example outputs, aggregate metrics, seed, model_hash, config_id, runtime_profile.

Example CLI: 
```
# run entire prompt set against model (float32)
eval-harness run --model s3://models/llama-3-13b/float32 --prompt-set ps_qa_support_001 --seed 42 --out s3://redwood-evals/results/llama-3-13b/ps_qa_support_001/2026-11-01
```

Required harness config fields (table):

| config_field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| model | S3 path or registry id | s3://models/llama-3-13b/float32 |
| batch_size | inference batch size used | 1 (latency tests) / 32 (throughput) |
| seq_len | sequence length cap for run | 512 |
| seed | RNG seed | 42 |
| quantization_profile | optional id if running quantized artifact | qp_llama3_13b_int8_v1 |

Quantization profiling & acceptance

- Profiles: quantization profiles capture per-layer scale factors, calibration datasets, and fallback rules. Store profiles in /data/eval/quantization-profiles with id qp_{model}_{scheme}_{version}.
- Procedure: 1) generate calibration dataset (min 2k representative prompts), 2) run calibration with noise injection, 3) produce profile and artifacts, 4) run eval-harness against quantized model.
- Acceptance thresholds (default):
  - Task-level metric drop <= 3% absolute or <= 5% relative (whichever is stricter).
  - Fluency / hallucination checks: no increase in hallucination rate > 2 percentage points.
  - Latency improvement >= 15% for target deployment (if latency is a driver).
  - No OOMs or unrecoverable runtime errors.

Quality guardrails

- Guardrail categories: Safety (toxicity, PII leakage), Correctness (factuality, task accuracy), Stability (variability under context), Performance (latency, memory).
- Implementations: small automated classifiers (safety-checker v2), behavioral tests (e.g., jailbreak suites), and manual review signoff for high-risk deployments.
- Guardrail gates: must be green on staging before any canary rollout. If any safety gate fails, model rollback is mandatory.

Regression detection & triage playbook

Triggers (automated):
- Any regression on primary metric beyond threshold (see Quantization acceptance).
- New crash / OOM during evaluation.
- Safety classifier failure rate increases by >1pp (percentage point) on critical prompt sets.

Triage steps (numbered):
1. Triage start: within 2 hours of detection, alert applied-ml and model owner via Slack alert channel #eval-triage and open a JIRA triage ticket with eval artifacts attached.
2. Initial assessment (8 hours): determine whether regression is due to infra, harness config, random seed, data drift, quantization artifact, or model weights. Reproduce with seed and float baseline.
3. Root cause (24-48 hours): run targeted experiments: ablation runs, per-layer quantization toggles, attention kernel sampling, and compare logits/differences.
4. Mitigation: either revert quantized artifact, adjust quantization parameters, or schedule model rollback with product. Document decisions in JIRA and update eval registry with resolution.
5. Postmortem: if incident caused customer impact or SLA breach, run standard incident postmortem (see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems).

Escalation matrix

- Critical: customer-impacting regressions or safety failures -> notify Eng SRE and Product immediately; target time-to-fix 8 hours.
- High: internal regression that blocks rollout -> applied-ml + model owner, target 48 hours.
- Medium/Low: non-blocking metric drift -> backlog grooming.

Reporting & dashboards

- Required dashboards: per-model eval summary (pass/fail, delta vs baseline), per-prompt-set histograms, quantization delta heatmaps, safety classifier trends. Owners: applied-ml + eng-platform.
- Storage: all eval outputs and metadata must be versioned in s3://redwood-evals/results/{model}/{prompt-set}/{timestamp}/manifest.json and indexed in eval-registry (internal service).

Templates & artifacts to attach to onboarding ticket

- Model card (required)
- Baseline eval report (float32)
- Prompt set id and sample prompts (at least 200)
- Quantization profile id(s) and calibration dataset link
- Safety checklist and manual review notes (if applicable)

Appendix: quick debugging checklist

- Re-run baseline with identical seed to ensure reproducibility.
- Compare per-example logits between float and quantized runs (diff threshold > 1e-3).
- Check runtime logs for truncated inputs, tokenization inconsistencies, or missing special tokens.
- Validate calibration dataset coverage: if non-representative, regenerate with stratified sampling.
